title: Errores típicos del hispanohablante
intro: Un hilo transversal con los fallos que más cometemos los hispanohablantes por calcar el español. Cada epígrafe muestra el error y su arreglo: ✗ incorrecto → ✓ correcto. Detectarlos y corregirlos es el atajo más rápido para sonar natural.

sections.title: Falsos amigos que cambian el sentido
sections.rule: Palabras que se parecen al español pero significan otra cosa. Los más peligrosos: actually = en realidad (no 'actualmente' → currently); sensible = sensato (no 'sensible' → sensitive); assist = ayudar/asistir a; embarrassed = avergonzado (no 'embarazada' → pregnant); realize = darse cuenta. Un falso amigo puede cambiar por completo el mensaje.

examples.en: ✗ I'm reading a book actually. → ✓ I'm currently reading a book. (actualmente)
✗ She's very sensible to criticism. → ✓ She's very sensitive to criticism. (sensible)
examples.es: Es muy sensible a las críticas.

examples.en: ✗ I'm embarrassed, I'm expecting a baby. → ✓ I'm pregnant. (embarazada)
✗ I assisted to the meeting. → ✓ I attended the meeting. (asistir a)
✗ Go to the library to buy a book. → ✓ Go to the bookshop. (librería)
examples.es: Ve a la librería a comprar un libro.

examples.en: ✗ The exit was a success. → ✓ The event was a success. (éxito)
✗ I have to record to call him. → ✓ I have to remember to call him. (recordar)
✗ He's a sympathetic person. → ✓ He's a nice / friendly person. (simpático)
✗ Actually I live in Madrid. → ✓ Currently / At the moment I live in Madrid.
✓ Actually, the price includes breakfast. (=en realidad, corrige)
examples.es: En realidad, el precio incluye el desayuno.

produce.label: tu turnoEscribe una frase correcta con actually (=en realidad) y otra con currently (=actualmente), para fijar la diferencia.
produce.placeholder: Ej: Actually, breakfast is included. I'm currently working on the report.
rubric: ¿Usas 'actually' con el sentido de 'en realidad / de hecho'?

notes.text: El más traicionero: actually ≠ actualmente. Actually = 'en realidad' (corrige o matiza); 'actualmente' = currently / at present. Y 'embarrassed' (avergonzado) ≠ 'pregnant' (embarazada): este error da lugar a situaciones cómicas.

sections.title: Orden de palabras
sections.rule: El inglés es rígido con el orden. Reglas que rompemos por calcar el español: (1) el adjetivo va ANTES del sustantivo (a red car, no 'a car red'); (2) no se separa verbo y objeto con un adverbio (I speak English well, no 'I speak well English'); (3) en preguntas se invierte con auxiliar (Where do you live?, no 'Where you live?'); (4) sujeto explícito siempre (It's raining, no 'Is raining').

examples.en: ✗ a car red → ✓ a red car
✗ I speak well English. → ✓ I speak English well.
✗ I like very much this hotel. → ✓ I like this hotel very much.
✗ Where you work? → ✓ Where do you work?
✗ Is raining. → ✓ It's raining. (sujeto obligatorio)
✗ Always I confirm by email. → ✓ I always confirm by email.
✗ a big beautiful house → ✓ a beautiful big house (opinión antes que tamaño)
✗ She has a hair long. → ✓ She has long hair.
✗ Who did call? → ✓ Who called? (wh- sujeto, sin 'did')
✗ I have 30 years. → ✓ I am 30 years old.

produce.label: tu turnoCorrige mentalmente y escribe bien: tu edad, algo que se te da bien, y una pregunta con 'where' o 'when'.
produce.placeholder: Ej: I'm 28 years old. I speak English quite well. Where do you usually stay?
rubric: ¿Usas 'be' para la edad (I'm X, no 'I have X years')?
¿Colocas el adverbio sin separar verbo y objeto?
¿La pregunta lleva auxiliar (do/does) o inversión correcta?

notes.text: Dos calcos fatales: 'I have X years' (edad) → 'I'm X'; y omitir el sujeto ('Is raining') → el inglés casi nunca lo omite: 'It's raining', 'There is…', 'It's difficult'.

sections.title: Doble negación y negativos
sections.rule: En español encadenamos negativos ('no vi a nadie'); en inglés solo puede haber un negativo. Con un verbo negativo se usa any-, no 'no-': I didn't see anyone (no 'didn't see nobody'). Con nobody/nothing/never (ya negativos), el verbo va en afirmativo: Nobody came (no 'nobody didn't come'). Y cuidado: 'nunca' = never (sin otro 'not').

examples.en: ✗ I don't know nothing. → ✓ I don't know anything. / I know nothing.
✗ I didn't see nobody. → ✓ I didn't see anybody.
✗ Nobody didn't come. → ✓ Nobody came. (verbo afirmativo)
✗ I don't never lie. → ✓ I never lie.
✗ We don't have nothing available. → ✓ We have nothing available. / We don't have anything.
✗ There isn't nobody at the desk. → ✓ There's nobody at the desk. / There isn't anybody.
examples.es: No hay nadie en el mostrador.

examples.en: ✗ She never says nothing. → ✓ She never says anything.
✗ I don't want neither. → ✓ I don't want either. / I want neither.
✓ None of the rooms are ready. (un solo negativo)
✓ I hardly ever complain. (hardly ya es casi-negativo)

quiz.question: 5. Con un verbo negativo (didn't) se usa:

produce.label: tu turnoEscribe 'no hay nada disponible' de las dos formas correctas (una con 'don't…any', otra con 'nothing').
produce.placeholder: Ej: We don't have anything available. / We have nothing available.

notes.text: Regla de oro: un solo negativo por oración. O niegas el verbo y usas 'any-' (don't know anything), o usas la palabra negativa con verbo afirmativo (know nothing). Nunca los dos ('don't know nothing').

sections.title: do vs make · say vs tell
sections.rule: Dos pares que el español funde. make = crear/producir un resultado (make a decision, a mistake, a reservation, money, dinner); do = tareas y actividades (do your job, homework, the shopping, business, a favour). say = decir algo (say something, sin destinatario directo: 'say that…'); tell = decir A ALGUIEN (tell someone, +objeto: tell me the truth). Se dice 'tell a story/lie/joke' pero 'say a word'.

examples.en: ✗ do a decision → ✓ make a decision
✗ make my homework → ✓ do my homework
✗ do a mistake → ✓ make a mistake
✗ do a reservation → ✓ make a reservation
✗ make business → ✓ do business
✗ Can you do me a favour? → ✓ do me a favour (correcto)
✗ He said me that... → ✓ He told me that... / He said that...
✗ Tell 'hello' to her. → ✓ Say hello to her.
✗ Can you say me the time? → ✓ Can you tell me the time?
✓ Don't tell lies. She always tells the truth.
examples.es: No digas mentiras. Ella siempre dice la verdad.

rows: tell a story / a lie / a joke
He told me (that) he was tired.

quiz.question: 4. '¿Me puedes decir la hora?':
options: Can you say me the time?
Can you tell me the time?

produce.label: tu turnoEscribe una frase con make y otra con do, y una con tell (a alguien) y otra con say.
produce.placeholder: Ej: We made a reservation. I did a favour for a guest. She told me the news. He said it was fine.
rubric: ¿'make' se usa para crear/resultado y 'do' para tareas?
¿'say' se usa sin destinatario directo (o con 'to')?

notes.text: Truco: tell casi siempre lleva a quién (tell me/him); say no ('say that…', o 'say to me' con preposición). Y memoriza los bloques fijos de make/do: no hay lógica, es de memoria.

sections.title: for / since / during / ago
sections.rule: El grupo temporal que más confundimos. for + duración (for two hours, for years). since + punto de inicio (since 2020, since Monday), con presente perfecto. during + sustantivo, cuándo (during the meeting) — no expresa duración. ago + tiempo, con pasado simple, va al FINAL (two years ago). Error típico: 'since two hours' (→ for two hours), 'during two hours' (→ for two hours).

examples.en: ✗ I've worked here since two years. → ✓ I've worked here for two years.
✓ I've worked here since 2022. (punto de inicio)
✗ I studied during three hours. → ✓ I studied for three hours.
✓ Don't call during the meeting. (cuándo, + sustantivo)
✗ I arrived here since Monday. → ✓ I arrived on Monday. / I've been here since Monday.
examples.es: Llegué el lunes / Estoy aquí desde el lunes.

examples.en: ✗ I met him before two years. → ✓ I met him two years ago.
✗ Ago two days I called. → ✓ I called two days ago. (ago va al final)
✓ We've been waiting for an hour. (duración + perfecto continuo)
✓ She's been off since the accident. (desde un punto)
examples.es: Está de baja desde el accidente.

examples.en: ✓ It rained during the night but stopped hours ago.
examples.es: Llovió durante la noche pero paró hace horas.

quiz.question: 1. 'Llevo dos años aquí':
options: I've been here since two years.
I've been here for two years.

quiz.question: 3. 'Lo conocí hace dos años':
options: I met him before two years.
I met him two years ago.

produce.label: tu turnoEscribe cuánto tiempo llevas en algo con for y since, y algo que hiciste con ago.
produce.placeholder: Ej: I've worked here for three years. I've lived in Madrid since 2021. I started this job two years ago.
rubric: ¿'for' va con duración y 'since' con punto de inicio?
¿'ago' va al final con pasado simple?

notes.text: Los tres fallos estrella: 'since two hours' (→ for), 'during two hours' (→ for), y 'before two years' para 'hace' (→ two years ago). 'during' nunca expresa cuánto, solo cuándo.

sections.title: Preposiciones que no se traducen igual
sections.rule: Muchas preposiciones no coinciden con el español y hay que memorizarlas con el verbo/adjetivo: depend on (de), married to (con), listen to (—), arrive at/in (a), think of/about (en), dream of (con), good at (en), interested in (en). Ver también los bloques 02.5–02.9. Error típico: calcar la preposición española ('depend of', 'married with').

examples.en: ✗ It depends of you. → ✓ It depends on you.
✗ She's married with a doctor. → ✓ She's married to a doctor.
✗ Listen the music. → ✓ Listen to the music.
✗ We arrived to the hotel. → ✓ We arrived at the hotel. / arrived in Madrid.
✗ I'm thinking in you. → ✓ I'm thinking of/about you.
✗ I dream with travelling. → ✓ I dream of travelling.
✗ He's good in maths. → ✓ He's good at maths.
examples.es: Se le dan bien las mates.

examples.en: ✗ I'm interested on the offer. → ✓ I'm interested in the offer.
✗ Wait me here. → ✓ Wait for me here.
✗ Look the photo. → ✓ Look at the photo.

produce.label: tu turnoEscribe tres frases con depend on, think of/about y good at, cuidando la preposición.
produce.placeholder: Ej: It depends on availability. I'm thinking about the offer. She's very good at sales.
rubric: ¿Usas la preposición inglesa correcta (no el calco español)?

notes.text: No traduzcas la preposición: memoriza el bloque verbo/adjetivo + preposición. Los más repetidos: depend on (no 'of'), married to (no 'with'), arrive at/in (no 'to'), listen to y wait for (que en español no llevan nada).

sections.title: La -s, plurales e incontables
sections.rule: Tres descuidos frecuentes: (1) la -s de la 3ª persona en presente (he works, she has) — se nos olvida; (2) incontables que en español son plurales: information, advice, news, furniture, money, homework son SINGULARES incontables (the news is…, no 'are'); (3) 'people' ya es plural (people are, no 'people is'). Concordancia sujeto-verbo cuidada.

examples.en: ✗ He work here. → ✓ He works here.
✗ She have two rooms. → ✓ She has two rooms.
✗ The news are good. → ✓ The news is good.
✗ The informations are useful. → ✓ The information is useful.
✗ I need some advices. → ✓ I need some advice. / a piece of advice.
✗ People is waiting. → ✓ People are waiting.
✗ The money are on the table. → ✓ The money is on the table.
examples.es: El dinero está en la mesa.

examples.en: ✗ Everybody have arrived. → ✓ Everybody has arrived. (everybody = singular)
✗ My hairs are wet. → ✓ My hair is wet.
✓ Two pieces of luggage, three items of furniture.

produce.label: tu turnoEscribe tres frases correctas: una en 3ª persona (con -s), una con 'people are' y una con un incontable (news/advice/information + is).
produce.placeholder: Ej: She works at reception. People are waiting in the lobby. The information is on the website.
rubric: ¿Pones la -s en la 3ª persona del presente?

notes.text: Incontables singulares clave: news, information, advice, furniture, money, homework, progress → 'is', sin plural. Pero people es plural → 'are'. Y no olvides la -s de he/she/it en presente: es el error más frecuente al hablar rápido.

sections.title: Artículos: cuándo 'the' y cuándo nada
sections.rule: El uso de the difiere del español. NO se usa 'the' con: sustantivos en sentido general (I love Ø music, no 'the music'), la mayoría de nombres propios/países (Ø Spain), comidas (Ø breakfast), y con last/next (Ø last week). SÍ se usa 'the' para algo específico/único ya conocido (the manager, the sun). Error típico: 'the' de más por calcar el 'el/la' español.

examples.en: ✗ I love the music. → ✓ I love music. (en general)
✗ The dogs are loyal. → ✓ Dogs are loyal. (los perros en general)
✗ I live in the Spain. → ✓ I live in Spain.
✗ We had the breakfast at 8. → ✓ We had breakfast at 8.
✗ I saw her the last week. → ✓ I saw her last week.
✗ She goes to the work by car. → ✓ She goes to work by car.
✓ The manager will see you now. (específico, conocido)
✓ Please close the door. (concreta, la de aquí)
✗ Life is beautiful in the nature. → ✓ …in nature.
✓ I play the piano but I don't like Ø football. (instrumentos: the; deportes: Ø)
examples.es: Toco el piano pero no me gusta el fútbol.

rows: específico: the music at the party
the dinner we had last night

quiz.question: 5. ¿Cuándo SÍ se usa 'the'?
options: siempre que en español haya el/la

produce.label: tu turnoEscribe una frase general SIN 'the' (una afición, un país) y otra específica CON 'the' (algo concreto y conocido).
produce.placeholder: Ej: I love travelling and I live in Spain. The manager confirmed the booking.
rubric: ¿Evitas el 'the' de más por calcar el español?

notes.text: El error más común es poner 'the' de más por calcar 'el/la': 'I love THE music' → 'I love music'. Regla rápida: sentido general = sin 'the'; algo concreto que ambos ya identificamos = con 'the'.
